On June 26, 2026, she introduced the Nutrition Education and Chronic Disease Prevention in Community Health Centers Act of 2026, which would fund nutrition education and counseling at federally qualified health centers, with priority given to communities with high rates of food insecurity and diet-related chronic disease — a measure with indirect benefits for children's health. Harshbarger introduced the Nutrition Education and Chronic Disease Prevention in Community Health Centers Act of 2026, which would authorize HRSA to fund evidence-based nutrition education and counseling at community health centers, with priority for communities with high food insecurity. The bill aligns with the 'Make America Healthy Again' agenda she cited. Separately, Harshbarger's prior votes include support for the One Big Beautiful Bill Act and the Nutritious SNAP Act of 2025, which restricted SNAP-eligible foods and tightened eligibility. As of June 2026, approximately 100,000 Tennesseans have lost SNAP benefits since the law's July 2025 effective date, according to Tennessee Lookout reporting. No new votes or statements specifically on child nutrition programs were found in the June 14–29 window beyond the nutrition education bill introduction.

parental_support.details: No new statements or legislation from Rep. Her existing record includes a YES vote on the Tax Relief for American Families and Workers Act (HR 7024, Jan. 2024), which expanded the Child Tax Credit, and co-sponsorship of the Parents Bill of Rights Act. The nutrition education bill she introduced in late June 2026 has indirect relevance to family health outcomes but is not a parental-support measure per se.
